title: A Static for the Signal
premise: Juniper Marchetti, sole navigator of the derelict relay ship Vesper, has spent eleven years maintaining a beacon that broadcasts a false ceasefire between two fleets still technically at war. The beacon's signal is generated by the backups sleeping in the hold—copies of the original crew, including Juniper's own mother—whose dreaming minds keep the lie coherent. When a distress call arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Juniper discovers the beacon was never commissioned by any fleet: it was built by the backups themselves to buy time for something they buried in the ship's core. As both fleets converge on the Vesper, Juniper must choose between waking the backups and preserving the peace, ultimately sacrificing their own identity as an original by merging with their mother's backup to broadcast a truth strong enough to end the war rather than hide it.
about_author: Sebastian Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade maintaining lighthouse beacons along the Scottish coast before turning to fiction. Their work explores the quiet violence of infrastructure—the machines we trust to remember what we'd rather forget.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper performs the daily maintenance ritual on the beacon, speaking aloud to the sleeping backups in the hold as if they can hear. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: tender loneliness; we learn Juniper talks to one backup in particular—a woman whose voice matches recordings of their mother.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: A distress transmission arrives in Pre-Collapse Standard, a language extinct for two centuries. Juniper decodes it using the ship's archive and finds it references the Vesper by name—and by a registry number that shouldn't exist. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread; invisibility was a choice someone else made for them.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper descends into the backup vault and discovers logs embedded in the stasis systems: the backups have been editing the beacon's message in their sleep, subtly rewriting history each cycle. POV: Juniper with interpolated backup-log fragments. Emotional beat: vertigo—the peace Juniper maintained may be a story the dead tell themselves.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Juniper intercepts fleet traffic revealing both armadas are converging on the Vesper, each believing the beacon confirms their own victory terms. The distress caller, salvage pilot Oren Vasquez, docks seeking refuge and recognizes the language as his grandmother's. POV: alternating Juniper/Oren. Emotional beat: wary alliance; Oren's grief mirrors Juniper's isolation.

chapters.title: Registry Zero
chapters.summary: Oren helps Juniper crack the sealed core, finding the truth: there was no commissioning order. The original crew built the beacon during the war's final hours to freeze both fleets in stalemate, then backed themselves up to power it forever. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into awe—the lie was an act of desperate love.

chapters.title: The Mother Backup
chapters.summary: Juniper initiates limited contact with the backup matching their mother, who wakes partially and reveals the core holds a genuine ceasefire framework the fleets' command structures suppressed. She asks Juniper to finish what the originals started. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: devastating intimacy; the mother remembers dying but not having a child.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Both fleets arrive and demand the Vesper surrender its beacon. A boarding action breaches the hull while Oren pilots evasive maneuvers through debris. Juniper must choose: shut down the beacon and let fleets collide, or wake all backups and lose the signal entirely. POV: Oren primarily. Emotional beat: panic and sacrifice; Oren takes damage covering Juniper's retreat to the core.

chapters.title: Waking the Choir
chapters.summary: Juniper wakes the backups en masse. Forty-seven minds flood the ship's systems, arguing, grieving, remembering. The beacon falters; fleet weapons arm. The mother backup proposes the impossible option: a single consciousness must carry the full truth into the broadcast, and it will not survive intact. POV: Juniper amid chorus voices. Emotional beat: overwhelming communion and terror.

chapters.title: A Static for the Signal
chapters.summary: Climax. Juniper merges with their mother's backup, becoming a hybrid voice that broadcasts the true ceasefire terms plus the record of the original crew's sacrifice—in both living languages and the extinct one. Both fleets receive proof their commands falsified the war's end. Weapons stand down as the truth propagates. POV: dissolving first-person plural. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-erasure.

chapters.title: Carrier Wave
chapters.summary: Resolution. The merged consciousness persists as the beacon's new voice—not Juniper, not the mother, something new. Oren, recovering aboard the repaired Vesper, becomes the ship's keeper and teaches the fleets' children the extinct language so the signal is never again unreadable. POV: Oren, closing letter to Juniper. Emotional beat: mournful hope; inheritance means carrying someone forward, not replacing them.
